_comment: Where the hands go on each weapon, in the fitted model's own space. Read by BOTH packages/core/src/modules/hassault/arms.ts and apps/native-fps/src/arms.rs (include_str!), and pinned together by apps/native-fps/tests/browser_parity.rs. NOT served: an anchor is a fact about the model rather than about the weapon's balance, so putting it in weapons.py would give the simulation's table a rendering column and hand it the response_model failure mode for nothing. Coordinates are cube units, x right / y up / z forward-negative — the same space build() and fitWeaponModel() leave a weapon in. Only exceptions are listed; anything absent is measured from the fitted bounding box by defaultGrips(), so a weapon added later looks plausible rather than empty-handed.

defaults._comment: Fractions of the weapon's own fitted bounding box, in the spirit of fitWeaponModel: derived rather than tuned, so a new weapon gets hands without anybody hand-placing them. `primary` is the trigger hand, back of centre and below the bore; `support` is the off hand, forward on the handguard.

pistol._comment: One hand on the grip and the other cupped under it — a pistol is held, not shouldered, so the support hand comes back and in rather than reaching down a handguard.

shotgun._comment: The support hand is on a pump, which sits lower and further forward than a rifle's handguard — and is where the reload animation's whole motion happens.

sniper._comment: Longest of the four, so the support hand is furthest out; the trigger hand sits further back behind a longer receiver.

knife._comment: One hand only. `support` is null rather than an off-screen coordinate: an empty hand is a real state, and a hand parked somewhere arbitrary is a hand the player will eventually see.
